conventions.convention: Use SI length coordinates x⁰=ct, signature (−,+,+,+), coordinate orientation dx⁰∧dx¹∧dx²∧dx³, and future unit observer n=H∂₀, with spatial orthonormal frame eᵢ=H⁻¹∂ᵢ.
Assume indexed AC_ω. The constants c, μ₀ and G_N are positive; ε₀=(μ₀c²)⁻¹, κ=8πG_N/c⁴, and Q_s is the positive square root of 4πε₀G_N.
The adopted sourced Maxwell sign is ∇ₐF^{ab}=−μ₀jᵇ, with F=dA, Eᵢ=cF(eᵢ,n), and matter force density Fᵇ{}_c jᶜ.
H is smooth and strictly positive on an open D⊆ℝ³, with ΔH≤0. Force and continuity equations remain undivided at zero density; σ/ρ is defined only where ρ>0.
Proper mass and signed charge use the induced spatial measure dV_h=H³dλ₃. They are not identified with ADM mass or measured quantities.
Dilute metric bounds are entrywise in the stated Cartesian chart, with a=δb and 0<δ≤1; the numerical example restricts this to 0<δ≤1/10.

load_bearing.statement: Under indexed AC_ω and the selected smooth SI charged-dust model, every smooth positive H on open D⊆ℝ³ with ΔH≤0 gives the displayed exact coupled solution, including the zero-density set. For H=1+a/√(r²+b²), a,b>0, the density is everywhere positive, M_prop=c²a/G_N, Q_prop=sQ_sc²a/G_N, and S_g=−2ΔH/H³>0. For a=δb, 0<δ≤1, the entrywise temporal, spatial and relative-density discrepancies are bounded by 3δ², δ² and 3δ respectively.

Assuming AC_ω, smooth positive H with ΔH≤0 and the stated constants and sign give smooth normalized charged-dust fields satisfying the formal sourced and homogeneous Maxwell equations, matter exchange and the Λ=0 Einstein equation; the total stress satisfies WEC, NEC, SEC and DEC.

Assuming AC_ω, the profile H=1+a/√(r²+b²), a,b>0, has ΔH=−3ab²/(r²+b²)^(5/2), positive density, finite proper mass c²a/G_N and signed charge sQ_sc²a/G_N, positive scalar curvature, and the stated dilute metric and density bounds.

Adopt the smooth Einstein–Maxwell equations with T_m^{ab}=ρUᵃUᵇ, jᵃ=σUᵃ, ρ≥0, future timelike U normalized by g(U,U)=−c², σ=0 wherever ρ=0, undivided mass continuity and Lorentz-force balance, and charge-current conservation.
